https://rochdale.gov.uk/news/article/662.title: Sunshine and smiles: Dreams come true at Rochdale Feel Good Festival – Rochdale Borough Council
https://rochdale.gov.uk/news/article/662.snapshot: Sunshine and smiles: Dreams come true at Rochdale Feel Good Festival – Rochdale Borough Council Thousands packed Rochdale town centre in the summer sunshine. Thousands packed Rochdale town centre in the summer sunshine on Saturday, 8 August 2026 for Rochdale Feel Good Festival. The town centre was filled with a feast of music, food and entertainment for the Rochdale Development Agency organised event, headlined by 2-time BRIT Award winner and pop/soul icon Gabrielle, Ash and Starsailor. The town centre was busy from early afternoon, with large crowds gathering at the main stage on Rochdale Town Hall Square. Councillor Georgina Jacques, assistant cabinet member for communities and co-operation at Rochdale Borough Council, said: “Following the OMD Summer of Hits concert on Friday night Rochdale Feel Good Festival brought a day of superb live music to town. We had visitors from right across the UK, some visiting Rochdale for the first time, and feedback has been very positive. Gabrielle was amazing and I think her set was a fitting celebration by a much-loved star, with lots of 90s nostalgia and feel good vibes in a stunning setting. Thanks to everyone who came along, the staff and partners who helped deliver it, our wonderful volunteers and the security crew and of course everyone who bought tickets. Thank you all for your support. Rochdale Development Agency are looking at feedback and carrying out a thorough evaluation in the coming weeks.” Councillor Georgina Jacques, assistant cabinet member for communities and co-operation at Rochdale Borough Council. The main stage hosted by DJ Dave Sweetmore was opened by local 5-piece metal band Metro, who won this year's Rochdale Music Service Battle of the Bands competition. It was an impressive debut that got a great reception from the crowd for the young band, who only formed last year. https://rochdale.gov.uk/news/article/666.title: Rochdale steps up its heritage offer with restoration of local landmark – Rochdale Borough Council
https://rochdale.gov.uk/news/article/666.snapshot: Rochdale steps up its heritage offer with restoration of local landmark – Rochdale Borough Council The restoration of a unique set of historic steps has been completed. The restoration of a unique set of historic steps which are more than 4 centuries old has been completed in the heart of Rochdale town centre. Running through the Broadfield Park Slopes, the Packer Spout steps link the major historic attractions of Rochdale Town Hall and its surrounding area to St Chad’s Church, the oldest church in the borough, parts of which have Saxon origins. Dating from sometime before 1660, the church steps have a rich history and were thought to be used by mourning relatives who would travel up the steps to St Chad’s Church, where they would scatter rue and rosemary in ‘God’s Acre’ (St Chad’s Churchyard) as an offering to ease the spirits of their loved ones. Situated in the recently restored Broadfield Park Slopes area, during the Victorian period, the steps ran directly through a notorious slum area, known as ‘the gank’. The gank was characterised by tightly packed housing, narrow passageways, high crime rates and large numbers of ‘houses of ill repute’. Many of the residents who worked in Rochdale’s mills would have lived out their lives in this area. The site is so steep that Oldham contractors, Maysand, who delivered the work, had to devise a special pulley system with tracks and rollers to help transport the stone up the hill. The team had to painstakingly remove all 122 steps, many of which had become broken and uneven, before reconstructing both the area underneath and the damaged steps using traditional sandstone, to match the existing stone. All materials that were salvageable were recycled and used to help reconstruct the steps. A new handrail was also created. Councillor Danny Meredith cabinet member for regeneration at Rochdale Borough Council, said: “I’m pleased to see another slice of Rochdale’s fascinating history painstakingly restored in the heart of our town centre conservation area. These steps have been part of the Rochdale landscape for many centuries and are a focal point of this stunning area. Combined with the beautifully restored Rochdale Town Hall and Square and the Broadfield Park Slopes, these are the final piece of this jigsaw and they look fantastic.”

https://rochdale.gov.uk/news/article/667.title: Don’t lose your vote - residents reminded to check voter registration details – Rochdale Borough Council
https://rochdale.gov.uk/news/article/667.snapshot: Don’t lose your vote - residents reminded to check voter registration details – Rochdale Borough Council Residents should check their electoral registration details or risk losing their chance to vote. The borough's residents are being urged to check their electoral registration details or risk losing their chance to vote on decisions that affect them. With local elections taking place in May 2027, it's an opportunity for residents to make sure they can take part. The annual canvass allows Rochdale Borough Council to keep the electoral register up to date, to identify who risks losing their voice at elections, and encourage them to register before it’s too late. Edward McCreadie, elections manager at Rochdale Borough Council, said: “Over the summer we've sent emails to residents in over 40,000 properties asking them to check their details and update if necessary and this week follow up letters were sent, so do keep an eye out. The annual canvass is our way of making sure that the information on the electoral register for every address is accurate and up to date. To make sure you don’t lose your say at upcoming elections, simply follow the instructions sent to you. If you’re not currently registered, your name will not appear in the messages we send. If you want to register, the easiest way is at rochdale.gov.uk/RegisterToVote." Local elections will be taking place in May 2027. Recent home movers, in particular, are urged to check their details. Electoral Commission research has found that recent home movers are less likely to be registered than those who have lived at the same address for a long time. In Great Britain, 92% of those who have lived in their home for 16 years will be registered, compared with 36% of people who have lived at an address for less than a year. Residents aged 16 and above can be added to the electoral register, but they can't vote until they are 18.

https://rochdale.gov.uk/news/article/674.title: International exchange: Middleton goes wild for nature inspired mural – Rochdale Borough Council
https://rochdale.gov.uk/news/article/674.snapshot: International exchange: Middleton goes wild for nature inspired mural – Rochdale Borough Council Artists from Rochdale and Kenya have brought a huge new endangered wildlife themed mural to Brook House in Middleton. Drivers and pedestrians in Middleton town centre are noticing some new wildlife popping up along their commute. Artists from Rochdale and Samburu, Kenya have brought a huge new endangered wildlife themed mural to Brook House on Oldham Road, encouraging residents to understand the importance of ecosystems as well as the conservation efforts that enhance wildlife and protect the planet. Lead artists - AYLO (Hayley Garner) from Rochdale and Kenyan based Victoria Firth, founder of global arts initiative The Wild Mural Project have been mentoring local artist Jamie Buckley and Kenyan based Ninah Tanya, to create their first international masterpiece in Middleton. Hayley, curator of the Common Walls International Mural Festival that has transformed public spaces with large-scale artwork in Rochdale said: "Victoria and I came up with the idea of 'Endangered Exchange' - an international collaboration that could create vibrant community driven art that inspires a deeper connection between people and the planet. It's not just painting, it's about developing artists and giving opportunities they might never otherwise have had, connecting communities across the world and showing how creativity can bring people together." A large heath butterfly - classed as endangered in the UK features in the artwork. Developed in partnership with the Lancashire Wildlife Trust, the Endangered Exchange initiative follows 'The Herds', the groundbreaking public art project that visited Heywood last year as part of Manchester International Festival and Rochdale's year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture, encouraging communities to renew their bond with the natural world. The striking 15 metre high x 10 metre wide mural features species that tell an interconnected story: a Hen Harrier, large heath butterfly - classed as endangered in the UK, emperor dragon fly, sphagnum moss that holds water and allows peat to form, and wildfires. Referencing the projects connection to Keyna, the phrase 'Save our tomorrow today' is written in Swahili - a call to notice what is around us, understand how connected it all is and to protect these landscapes before the warning becomes a loss we cannot reverse. The new mural has been designed to represent mounting pressure being placed on landscapes that may appear strong but are held together by delicate relationships between water, plants, insects, birds and climate. The artwork also features Kanga, a striking fabric that reflects the rich culture of Keyna.

https://rochdale.gov.uk/news/article/682.title: On record: Rochdale’s new album celebrates town’s music history – Rochdale Borough Council
https://rochdale.gov.uk/news/article/682.snapshot: On record: Rochdale’s new album celebrates town’s music history – Rochdale Borough Council An album of iconic music recorded in Rochdale by local artists has already reached millions of listeners on national radio. An album of iconic music recorded in Rochdale by local artists has already reached millions of listeners on national radio and thousands more on streaming platforms. A single off the record made the UK official charts, alongside a stack of glowing reviews. Launched as part of Rochdale’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture and released on vinyl and digital platforms this summer the album ‘Kenion Street’ featured local acts performing their version of a classic track originally recorded at Cargo or Suite Sixteen studios in Rochdale. Cover artwork for ‘Kenion Street,’ an album of iconic music recorded in Rochdale by local artists. The borough boasts a rich musical legacy, from Gracie Fields to Lisa Stansfield, and more recently The Courteeners. Between 1977- 2001 Rochdale was home to both Suite Sixteen and Cargo Studios on Kenion Street, where trailblazing artists including OMD, The Stone Roses, Happy Mondays, Joy Division, Inspiral Carpets, Autechre, A Certain Ratio, The Fall and many others recorded some of their most memorable work. PoolEra perform Electricity by OMD, another classic track originally recorded in Rochdale. The 11 tracks on ‘Kenion Street’ included PoolEra’s version of Electricity by OMD, Dreams Never End by New Order re-imagined by Medley, and Jennifer Read’s dramatic version of Totally Wired, by The Fall. All the new tracks were recorded and produced at Voltalab Sound Studios, based in the original Cargo/Suite Sixteen building on Kenion Street, by studio founder Jamie Alsop. Radio 6 Music also featured the album, playing Middleton band’s K-Estate's version of Gang of Four’s Damaged Goods. It was also made Track of the Day on Radio X with other tracks played across XS Manchester, Mersey Radio, Phoenix FM and many more, with a combined audience of over 3.5 million.

https://rochdale.gov.uk/news/article/688.title: Rochdale crowned Britain in Bloom champion after striking gold – Rochdale Borough Council
https://rochdale.gov.uk/news/article/688.snapshot: Rochdale crowned Britain in Bloom champion after striking gold – Rochdale Borough Council Rochdale is celebrating after striking gold at this year’s Britain in Bloom awards. Rochdale is celebrating a blooming brilliant victory after striking gold at this year’s Britain in Bloom awards and being crowned the overall winner of the Town Centres and City Centres category. Rochdale was placed ahead of Floral Godalming (Southeast), Shaftesbury in Bloom (South) and Sidcup Partners Limited (London). Rochdale in Bloom has a proud competition record, securing gold in 2018, being named Best Small City in 2022 and winning gold again for Rochdale town centre in 2024. This year’s category win keeps the title in the borough after Middleton town centre took the top prize last year. Rochdale has undergone significant regeneration in recent years. The Grade I-listed Rochdale Town Hall has been expertly restored, complemented by the creation of the new Town Hall Square and the transformation of the Broadfield Park slopes. Supported by a multi-million-pound National Lottery Heritage Fund grant, have made this historic quarter the envy of many. Judges praised Rochdale town centre’s vibrant displays from Bowlee Garden Nursery, recycling initiatives and exceptional cleanliness, as well as the pride, teamwork and dedication of everyone involved. They also recognised the commitment to local biodiversity and strong partnerships, with Rochdale exceeding the gold standard in horticulture, environmental responsibility and community participation. Rochdale’s historic Baillie Street Quarter and striking murals, created through the 2025 Rochdale Common Walls Festival, strengthened the town centre’s entry by showcasing its culture and civic pride. Councillor Tricia Ayrton, deputy leader and cabinet member for climate change and environment at Rochdale Borough Council, said: “What another outstanding achievement for our borough. Last year, Middleton town centre achieved gold and was overall category winner and now Rochdale town centre is back as a worthy winner once again championing our borough for 2026.

https://rochdale.gov.uk/news/article/689.title: Wheels fall off for drivers who failed to stop for Heywood school crossing patrol – Rochdale Borough Council
https://rochdale.gov.uk/news/article/689.snapshot: Wheels fall off for drivers who failed to stop for Heywood school crossing patrol – Rochdale Borough Council 2 drivers who failed to stop for a school crossing patrol have had their vehicles seized by police. 2 irresponsible drivers who failed to stop for a school crossing patrol in Bury Old Road have had their vehicles seized by police. The incidents took place on Tuesday, 13 and Wednesday, 14 October 2026, with school crossing patrol, Barry, having to move out of the way to avoid the vehicles, a moped and a silver Skoda, even though he was already standing in the road. Fortunately, nobody was injured in the incident. The matter was reported to police, who used new powers under section 59 of the police reform act 2002, to seize the vehicles after collecting evidence, including witness statements. Cars and other vehicles failing to stop for school crossing patrols is a growing problem, with 137 fail to stops reported across Rochdale borough over the past 5 years. Body worn cameras are now being used in hotspot areas to try to deter dangerous driving and support prosecutions where needed. Councillor Dylan Williams, cabinet member for highways and facilities, said: “It beggars belief that somebody would see a school crossing patrol clearly standing in the middle of the road and continue to drive. Frankly I’m appalled. “We would like to thank GMP for their quick and decisive action and I think it’s a really good result.

https://rochdale.gov.uk/news/article/687.title: Rochdale Town Hall’s feted restaurant scoops international award – Rochdale Borough Council
https://rochdale.gov.uk/news/article/687.snapshot: Rochdale Town Hall’s feted restaurant scoops international award – Rochdale Borough Council The restaurant has picked up the Trip Advisor Travellers’ Choice Award 2026. Rochdale Town Hall’s Martlet Kitchen has picked up the Trip Advisor Travellers’ Choice Award 2026, placing it among the top-rated restaurants in the world on the popular review site. The award honours businesses which consistently receive great reviews, with their scores placing them in the top 10 per cent of all establishments registered on the popular review site. With millions of businesses from around the globe listed on the site, the award is a huge accolade for the Martlet Kitchen, which recently celebrated its second birthday. It’s not the first time the restaurant, which specialises in traditional, high-quality British food, has been lauded. In his food column for The Guardian, legendary food critic Jay Rayner, described the Martlet Kitchen as a ‘victory of professionalism, good sense and, most of all, great taste and skill’ when he visited shortly after its opening in 2024. The Martlet Kitchen is helmed by multi award winning chef, Darren Parkinson, who trained at Hopwood Hall College before working at acclaimed establishments including Shibden Mill Inn in Halifax and the Fleece Inn in Ripponden, both of which boast 2 AA rosettes. Rooted in the community, its food and drink is sourced from the local area, including Milnrow’s Jacksons Farm, Defiance Distillery at Spotland Mill and Grandpa Greene’s in Oldham. “This award is great news and we’re aiming for more accolades in the future. It’s about good old fashioned British grub, cooked to perfection, using top quality local ingredients, coupled with excellent service.”
